newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEEKEND PROGRAMME IN THE SPANISH LEAGUE CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: The following matches are scheduled to take place this weekend in the Spanish league championship:
(league position in parentheses; all kickoff times gmt)
Last year's surprise outfit, Compostela, are struggling this year while Vicente Cantatore's Valladolid have picked up after narrowly avoiding relegation last season.
First division new-boys Extremadura, who are close to breaking the record for the worst-ever league start, face a troubled side that is still without defender Quique Flores.
Tenerife will hope to score their first-ever victory in the San Mames stadium, where fallen giants Athletic will be without defender Bixente Lizarazu.
Real's unbeaten record is on the line after a flu bug that could leave them without midfielder Fernando Redondo and striker Raul Gonzalez for this top of the table clash.
Despite a mixed home record Deportivo are clear favourites against an Espanyol side that was trounced 3-0 at home by Feyenoord in the UEFA Cup on Tuesday.

Newly-promoted Hercules haven't won a point since a win on the first day of the season. Since then they have lost six on the trot and take on Oviedo, a side that tends to be at their best away from home.
Racing looked strong against Real Madrid last week and have striker Alberto Lopez back from suspension, but Russian midfielder Sergie Shustikov is out through injury.
Betis tend to give away at home what they win away, while Rayo's Brazilian goalscorer Guilherme is doubtful after damaging his right foot in training.
Barcelona welcome back brilliant Brazilian striker Ronaldo from international duty while goalkeeper Vitor Baia is fully recovered from injury.
Atletico are missing vital midfielder Jose Luis Caminero for a fixture that produced some classic matches in both Cup and league last season.
Sporting will hope to pick up three points against troubled --- and unlucky -- Sevilla before facing big-boys Valencia, Atletico Madrid and Barcelona in consecutive games.
